messages.subject: AW: [DIST-SAMP] Generating an estimate of expected cluster size
parts:
Dear Brendan, Jeff, list,

I reported a problem to the list on april 12, which only occurred with =
one
dataset. The range of observed cluster size in that dataset is nearly as
large as in Brendan's (2 - 6,500). The problem was, that in CDS the =
analytic-
and the bootstrap-estimator for the CV of the estimation of the mean =
cluster
size E(s) produced quite different results (8.6 % vs. 29.6 %).

Brendan:
I'm wondering whether you observed the same discrepancy in the =
estimators as
I did - maybe the high variability in cluster sizes is the reason for =
this
problem?!=20

Jeff:
Your proposal of using ln(cluster size) as a covariate in MCDS sounds =
quite
promising for me, but I don't completely understand how exactly this =
should
work...=20
I already tried to use cluster size as a covariate in MCDS, so that the
density of individuals D can be obtained directly from the
Horvitz-Thompson-like estimator.=20
Is the idea to use ln(cluster size) in the same way? However, this would
*not* result in an estimation of D, but in an estimation of - well, I'm =
not
sure, but maybe something like ln(D)*DS ?!=20
Or was the idea to include ln(cluster size) as a covariate; but to =
estimate
E(s) independently by the mean size of observed clusters, so that D has =
to be
estimated by DS*E(s) ?

Best regards,=20
Tim

Betreff: Re: [DIST-SAMP] Generating an estimate of expected cluster size
given tremendous variance in sampled cluster size?

With that range of group sizes I'd be a little leery of the regression=20
approach even though it is using ln(group size). If it was me I'd focus =

on using ln(group size) as a covariate in mcds. Doing some simulation=20
may be helpful. I've never dealt with anything with that kind of=20
range.--jeff

On 7/27/2011 10:57 AM, Brendan Shirkey wrote:
> > Hello All,
> >
> > My name is Brendan Shirkey and I am graduate student trying to develop
aerial survey protocols for diving ducks using distance sampling =
techniques.
We have what I believe is a relatively unique problem in that we are =
dealing
with a clustered population (flocks of diving ducks) but these clusters =
range
in size from 1 individual to 20 or 30 thousand individuals. We are =
pleased
with the performance of the detection model; however we are bit torn =
with how
to determine expected flock size. Currently, we are using the option in
distance that takes the regression of the ln of flock size against g(x) =
in
order to account for the increased detection probability of larger =
groups.
We have also tried including flock size as a covariate, but I don't even =
know
if this is appropriate given the tremendous range in flock size. If =
anyone
has dealt with a similar problem in distance their insight would be much
appreciated. Specifically, we are wondering if anyone has any thoughts =
on
what might be the most statistically valid way of estimating expected =
flock
size in Distance given the tremendous variance we are dealing with. Any
suggestions or discussion would be much appreciated.
